findings.fixHint: Add a stable `data-composition-id` to the entry composition wrapper.
Set numeric `data-width` and `data-height` on the entry composition root.

findings.message: CSS declaration `transition: opacity 0.4s ease` runs on the browser clock and cannot be seeked deterministically across render workers.
findings.fixHint: Keep the class or attribute swap for state; put the visual change on the paused GSAP timeline.

findings.message: CSS declaration `transition: width 0.6s cubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)` runs on the browser clock and cannot be seeked deterministically across render workers.

findings.message: <audio id="sfx-tick"> has src but no data-start. HyperFrames cannot own playback for untimed media, so preview and render behavior can diverge.
findings.fixHint: Add data-start="0" (or the intended start time) and data-duration if the clip should stop before the source ends.

findings.message: Inline <script> imperatively controls managed media via play(). HyperFrames must own media play/pause/seek to keep preview, timeline, and renders deterministic.
findings.fixHint: Remove imperative media play/pause/currentTime/muted control. Express timing with data-start/data-duration and media offsets like data-media-start or data-playback-start instead.

findings.message: GSAP timeline is created but never registered in window.__timelines. The runtime discovers timelines from this registry. Without registration, animations will not play during preview or render.
findings.fixHint: Add `window.__timelines = window.__timelines || {};` and `window.__timelines["root"] = tl;` after creating the timeline (use the composition's data-composition-id as the key).

findings.message: GSAP tween on "#s2-scan-beam" uses motion that snaps to integer device pixels: top. Layout and text-reflow properties snap during browser layout; roundProps rounds the tween value. Slow motion or an ease-out tail then stutters under the seek-by-frame capture engine. Animate transforms (x/y/scale/opacity) instead.
findings.fixHint: replace top with the transform equivalent (y), e.g. tl.fromTo("#s2-scan-beam", { x: -1300 }, { x: 0, ...yourAnimation }). Transforms interpolate sub-pixel and stay smooth at any speed.

findings.message: `z-index: -1` paints the element behind its nearest stacking context's own content. With no stacking-context ancestor that context is the composition root itself, so an opaque background there hides it entirely: in the DOM, laid out, and absent from the picture. A transparent root leaves it visible. Siblings at `z-index: 0` or above are unaffected.
findings.fixHint: Give the element's parent a stacking context - `isolation: isolate` is the cheapest, and `transform`, `filter`, `opacity` below 1, `contain: paint` and `will-change` all work too. The negative-z child then paints above that parent's background and renders normally. Or express paint order through DOM order - an earlier sibling paints behind a later one - and raise the elements that should sit in front rather than lowering this one.
